items.q: Why is a wrong question worse in lending?
items.a: It can be a **regulatory issue**, not just a bad customer experience.

items.q: Give an example of a compliance trap.
items.a: If funds are for **medical purposes**, the agent **must not ask the amount**.
An **LLM-as-judge** runs after each call, with a yes/no compliance verdict and an explanation.

items.q: How far did judge-human agreement move?
items.a: From **33% to 92%**, by writing down **tribal knowledge**, settling reviewer disagreement and improving the judge.

items.q: How attached should you be to your first metrics?
items.a: **Not at all.** Drop metrics that don't matter and keep the ones that do.

items.q: Where should eval metrics come from?
items.a: From the **product definition** and what human reviewers actually label. "Evals are the product definition."
They go to **review queues** and are **routed to the owning team** (agent, compliance or engineering).
By **re-simulating voice-to-voice** (accents, noise, interruptions) before production.
No. Changes stay **behind feature flags** with **human and compliance sign-off**.
